names.display_en: Shi Hu, Martial Emperor of Later Zhao

summary: 石勒侄，废杀石弘自立，迁都邺，后赵武功极盛；然暴虐著称，营宫室、兴大役、好杀伐，死后诸子争立，后赵迅即崩溃。
summary_en: Nephew of Shi Le, he deposed and slew Shi Hong to take the throne, moved the capital to Ye, and carried Later Zhao to its height of power; but his tyranny is proverbial — palaces, corvée, and slaughter — and after his death his sons fought, and Later Zhao collapsed at once.

portrait.appearance_basis: 史载无形貌描写。画像宜表现雄武而暴戾的中老年君主之态，衣冠从后赵制。属艺术想象。

timeline.summary_en: Nephew of Shi Le, styled Jilong; a fierce warrior and one of Le's field commanders.

timeline.title: 废杀石弘自立
timeline.summary: 废弘自立，称居摄赵天王，后称帝。
timeline.summary_en: He deposed Hong and took power himself, calling himself Heavenly King of Zhao Regent, later emperor.

timeline.title: 迁都于邺
timeline.summary: 自襄国迁邺，大营宫殿苑囿。
timeline.summary_en: He moved the capital from Xiangguo to Ye and raised palaces and parks on a grand scale.

timeline.title: 大役与东宫
timeline.title_en: Great Works and the Eastern Palace
timeline.summary: 发民夫营宫室、猎场，史称百姓愁怨。
timeline.summary_en: He drove the people to build palaces and hunting grounds — the histories record their grief and rage.

timeline.title: 石虎崩
timeline.summary: 崩，诸子争立，后赵迅即崩溃。
timeline.summary_en: He died; his sons fought for the throne, and Later Zhao fell apart at once.

timeline.title: 季龙总评
timeline.summary: 史臣极言其虐；武功拓地与虐政并载。
timeline.summary_en: The historians dwell on his cruelty; his conquests and his tyranny are recorded together.

bio_md:
# 后赵武帝 · 主要事迹

石虎字季龙，石勒之侄。骁勇善战，为石勒方面大将，攻城略地，多出其力。咸和八年石勒崩，虎受遗辅石弘，旋专权；咸和九年，废杀石弘自立，称居摄赵天王，后称帝。石虎迁都于邺，大营宫殿苑囿，「发民夫四十余万」筑华林苑、猎场，又括民女充后宫，史称百姓愁怨。

石虎之暴，为十六国君主之最：役民无度，杀人如麻，「既而自以无子，复立其幼子」，诸子争立，骨肉相残；又发兵攻前燕、前凉，武功虽盛，而民力已竭。永和五年，石虎崩，诸子为争帝位自相残杀，石闵（冉闵）乘乱起兵，杀胡人二十余万，后赵迅即崩溃——其盛也暴，其亡也速。

史家论石虎：「季龙以凶戾之资，奋残暴之性，虽复冠带蛮貊，终为豺狼之德。」后赵之武功，尽丧于暴政；其「胡汉相杀」之祸，更为五胡之乱中最惨烈者。虎之兴亡，足为暴政亡国之鉴。

> 参考：点校本《晋书》卷106《石季龙载记》、卷107《石闵载记》。

bio_parts_en.value:
Shi Hu, styled Jilong, was the nephew of Shi Le, a fierce warrior who took cities for his uncle as one of his field commanders. In the 8th year of Xianhe Le died; Hu, by the late will, assisted Shi Hong — and at once seized power. In the 9th year he deposed and slew Hong and stood himself, calling himself Heavenly King of Zhao Regent, later emperor. He moved the capital to Ye, raised palaces and parks on a grand scale, and "drove over 400,000 laborers" to build the Huayuan park and hunting grounds; he swept the realm's women into his harem — the records say the people grieved and raged.

His tyranny was the worst of the Sixteen States: corvée without limit, slaughter without mercy; and with his sons contending, kin slew kin. He campaigned against Former Yan and Former Liang, his arms at their height while the people's strength ran out. In the 5th year of Yonghe he died; his sons fought for the throne, and Shi Min (Ran Min) rose in the chaos and slew over 200,000 Hu — Later Zhao collapsed at once. It rose in tyranny and fell in a moment.

The historians say of him: "With a savage nature and a brutal temper, though he put on the robes of civilization, his virtue was the wolf's." The realm's strength was spent in cruelty; and the Hu–Han slaughter of his fall was the bitterest of the barbarian age. His rise and ruin stand as the warning of tyranny.

> References: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 106 (records of Shi Jilong), ch. 107 (records of Shi Min).
